review_text: when I say LOST IN THE SAUCE for this class, I mean it beyond. not one single lecture did I come out understanding what was going on. this man was all over the place like spitting things left and right that just either didnt connect or were so confusing without any background knowledge. yes this man is so passionate and he loves this topic but let me tell you how annoying this class was. the tophat reading is so long and I highly doubt anyone ever read it but its supposed to help you understand whats going on in class so then when he teaches it in lecture you already have a foundation but like the readings are so long and also kinda confusing so by like the second week nobody actually reads them I feel like. the lab is the biggest joke of all time legit not clue what was flying the entire time and the lab reports are graded based on vibes it felt like, just hope you get a chill TA that doesn't make you do the dumb work sheet in the beginning of the class and you can just send that hour working on the lab instead. now let me tell you guys about the final the fact of the matter is that it kind of determines your entire grade, had a high A the entire semester and then did not do so well on the final and BOOM A- in the class overall even tho that doesn't actually represent how I truly did in the class. yea his curves are great but like sometimes not as much as they should be. Overall this guy is passionate but I came out knowing not one thing abt physics and with an annoying grade that doesn't represent how I did in the class.

Severson is an extremely lazy professor. You legitimately get nothing from going to the in-person lectures, he records them and leaves the TopHat clicker questions open for 48 hours. He consistently goes on his phone multiple times a lecture and you can really tell that he doesn’t want to be teaching the class. The curve is really generous. You can score significantly below the mean on the exams and still end with a B or B+ in the class. Overall, take this class if you want a good grade, but don’t expect to learn anything about physics. If you’re studying for the MCAT, you may want to consider going with another professor who’ll actually teach the class, otherwise you’re going to be stuck self-studying.
By no means is this class easy. Lectures are sometimes confusing but usually his exam material is pulled or extremely similar to homework or lecture.
the lab isnt bad. you legit never see severson tho. Its a pretty easy lab not gonna lie

I honestly have no idea why his score was so high. I feel like the way he structured the class was fairly disorganized at best and completely messy at worst. a) The homework felt "too easy" in a sense, to the point that I felt like I wasn't adequately prepared for the exams when going in. Not only that, but the exams were COMPLETELY multiple choice, which completely threw me off as someone who is used to having free-response physics exam for the bulk of my academic career. He gave no practice exams, nor did he indicate what the exams were going to be like. b) His lecture style can be very boring at times, and I sometimes felt like he was just giving us fun facts rather than actually teaching the course material. He shows that he is passionate about physics and what he teaches, but it doesn't translate well into what I actually needed to understand for his class. c) He has a very strange grading system where he normalizes the average grade, which basically means that he can curve you down! For me and a lot of my peers, he dropped us from two whole sign grades (those expecting a B got a C+, and those expecting a B- got a C), and it felt quite unexpected.

Professor Turpen is one of the kindest professors I have ever encountered. She genuinely cares about learning and allows students to redo exam/homework problems for partial credit which is really helpful for not only boosting your grade, but learning material in the class. It is a tough course, but she sets up students to succeed. That being said, my only complaint is that it takes forever to get grades back in this class. I still have ungraded assignments from September which is frustrating not having a solid clear grade going into finals. Aside from that, I loved taking 371 with her and could not recommend her more. I hope I get to take another class with her!
Do not take him. He is awful. Worst Professor of all time. He is mean. Bad! He ate my cheerios

Yakovenko is a instantly likeable professor. He's funny, smart, and he's definitely effective at communicating the material. He has a habit of dropping constants in equations, which is okay, but you will need to include them in the homework or lose points. Of course, the first couple of times he does it, he re-introduces them at the end, so you kind of learn to do it yourself. He adapted the course structure to the students' incoming knowledge very well, he answered any questions directly (though he sometimes missed the point of a question), and he rapidly responded to any questions you might email him. I personally had an incident where I was sick and emailed him asking if I could scan my homework and email to him. He said I could and said he would give it to the TA. The next week, it turned out that the TA never got my homework, and Yakovenko said that he was not a conduit to the TA and that he hadn't agreed to give the TA my homework, that I would have to go directly to the TA. I double checked the email, and I wasn't making up our conversation, so I was a little peeved. I gave the homework to the TA and it didn't get marked down for lateness though, so from a practical standpoint there wasn't really a problem. In the end, I am looking forward to having Yakovenko as a professor again in PHYS404, which I guess says more than the rest of this review.

Dr. Hall is a fantastic teacher. Everything is clear, concise, and on point with what you need to know. He keeps all his lectures and notes in a logical order and there's hardly confusion when reviewing over them again. Homeworks are from the textbook and are generally not too terribly difficult. Exams (take-home this semester) were tough, but doable. He's a bit of an android in terms of emotions or humor, but it's hilarious when he does joke. This is my second semester with him (previously PHYS 273) and I'd, without a doubt, take another class with him.

The class itself is super easy. He literally gives you formula sheets to use during tests, so you just plug the numbers in on the exam. He's just a little insufferable as a professor. Extremely strict attendance, assigned seating, etc etc. If you need a gpa boost, take this class. Just be prepared to roll your eyes at his bs every. single. day.

This guy really likes math. I mean really likes math. He goes on lots of tangents and tends to conceptualize things in a way that only makes sense if you read the textbook or if you're very tapped into math. Besides the fact that his teaching ability is below average, he does actually care about his students. He curves when necessary and gives you homeworks that are free points along with bonus points that you can go for to save your grade. If you actually study, you can succeed in this class but it is hard to learn from this guy. The only reason he gets 3 stars is because his fits are pretty fire.

bros the goat, easy class. easy A. thank god I took him. if he keeps this up, he's the obvious choice for 401. it's a basic requirement anyway, so the shortfalls of his class don't really matter. take Anurag, keep your sanity.

I want to start off this review by saying that the professor is a very nice guy. He genuinely has no malintent. However, there are certain shortcomings that took place during the course, which is rather unfortunate. I'll start with the most recent and move backwards in time. - The last two weeks have been conducted and have not been focused on our imminent final exam, rather, using R and its applications for statistics (material we are not assessed on). This honestly sucks, given the fact that it is unclear what exactly will be covered on the final. Again, the final we have in a few days. - Before these last two weeks, there was a total of three weeks where the professor was not present, and we had an alternate instructor. These instructors covered the most difficult material in the course, and since they do not directly oversee the exams, it was hard to understand what exactly was and wasn't exam-relevant. Now, he did provide legitimate reasoning as to why he was not able to attend our class, just not great, given out of the 15 weeks in the semester, we have not had substantive lectures for 5 of them. The biggest concern for me is what to study for the final. He gave us six files for practice problems, however, there are some content differences generally between this and the other final exams on the testbank. Would be nice to get some closure on what exactly I should be focusing on. Pros of the course: quizzes and exams are fair, if not helpful given they have been based off of practice exercises and we have been allowed to use a cheat sheet on the midterms and upcoming final. He is approachable and can be helpful.

Awesome, awesome professor. Weekly quizzes are fair and good practice. Homeworks are relevant for the most part, and on average difficult but not impossible. Exams are also incredibly fair, and there is a practice exam posted and a review session in the class before the exam. Dr. Danul is also a great lecturer. He talks slowly, explains topics well, and constantly pauses to make sure everyone is following along. He answers questions well, and my favorite thing he does is relate material to real-world applications. I would 100% recommend taking this course with Dr. Danul, and I wish I had taken more courses with him in the past.

Her sample exams are not a good representation of how actual exams are. Her exam 2 was very disorganised. It was no way a 50 minute exam. Her grading is also extremely harsh. The slides, HW and some exam questions are confusing and hard to understand. This is supposed to be an easy A class but she made it much harder. I have never gotten anything below a B in my entire college experience, yet I am close to failing this class.

Dr. G is a great professor. Her lectures are pretty entertaining, her exams are not super difficult, and she provides resources. For every exam, she gives her students a study guide in which she pulls questions/topics directly from what is on the study guide and she allows students to use the front and back of an index card on the exams. She doesn't do clicker questions anymore, like the past reviews say. She is very nice and I have friends who created meetings with her to discuss their grades and ask for help and she seemed very accommodating. There is a biodiversity project worth approximately 5% of your grade, which takes a maximum of 1 hour and is an easy 100%. The homeworks were usually wekly SimBio's due on friday at midnight that also did not take a lot of time. She also does not do any curves or rounding. The only thing I would say as a negative is that at the beginning of an exam (usually half multiple choice worth 5pts each, half free response) she would say to not write a lot in the free response section; however, she would take off points if you were not specific enough. Otherwise, she is super sweet, and you can tell she really wants her students to succeed. I would recommend her as a teacher.

This lab was a fucking shitshow. You're given no instructions on how to complete difficult homework. He leaves you completely in the dark. I'm not exaggerating when I say there are no instructions. Assignments will say "make x,y,z" with no further explanation on how to do so.
Such a great TA! GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS! He is so good at breaking down hard concepts and a genuinely nice person

This class is solely TA run, so your TA is really what matters for the class. The assignments can be annoying and long, but not too bad if your lab group is good. I was lucky enough to have Harriet Harris, who was awesome. My lab group was great, making this an overall enjoyable experience.

The cheat sheet is so clutch for this class in BSCI201. I usually make a Canva sheet in 5.5 font filled with all the topics covered + she gives extra credit for her exams, which has let me have 100% on all three midterms (I scored around a low A every time prior to extra credit). This let me have more time to study for the lab practicals, which I think are harder than the lecture exams because of the overwhelming amount of vocab you have to memorize. The lab is totally doable as long as you spam Quizlet or Anki over and over again FOR ALL THE THINGS LISTED ON THE STUDY GUIDE (yes its going to be a lot but u can do it) Good luck!

This teacher is not only the most selfish teacher I have ever had to deal with but also does not follow university policies. She is not accommodating nor does she care for her students I had the worst experience with her and she denied me of my accommodation except nothing but selfishness from her.

Carleton is a really nice professor, and I love that she records the lectures. You don't need to go to class as long as you watch lecture recordings. The class absolutely sucks, but if you're a bio major, you have to take it. Tests are based on the content she talks about. Frqs are based on GAEs. There is a small curve at the end, which can round your grade up.

ok so i definitely struggled in the beginning. the exams seemed really hard and everyone i knew was not doing well. her style of teaching is reading straight from 80 slides per class and often getting confused when doing her own examples. it's kinda frustrating but i've heard she's helpful in office hours. there was also a SLIGHT curve (like an 88.5 was made to be a A-). she records her lectures which is nice but almost no one showed up to class. she goes over warm up examples which are very close to the exam questions. honestly exams are more application than memorization which is why it's frustrating in the beginning. by the last midterm and final i had figured out a good way to study (LOTS of flashcards, warm ups, and topic quizzes). lab is a really good grade buffer (it's 25% of total grade) so do ur best on those bc it's easy. this class is doable with her but please try ur best from the beginning it's hard to recover after a few bad midterms, especially with little to no curve

At first i thought this was a good prof but there's so many assignments and projects on top of lab, and the hours you put in outside of class actually learning the material because of the flipped classroom is so stupid. the big thing is her unfairness with exams: apparently our average grade for the first exam was "too high" (it was a B-), because she basically sabotaged our second exam by putting way too much content and too many FRQs for the 50 mins given. I don't know a single person who finished that exam or felt good about it. And there's no curve despite all this negative feedback.

GOAT prof - tells you what he's going to ask on the exam in class. Doesn't change exams from previous yrs for the most part - get old exams and you'll have an A easy easy easy. Only annoying part is you have to go to class bc of clicker questions.

The content was very interesting, and lectures were well-done. However, exams were *very* hard. They simultaneously required memorization of many little details (memorize every word on those worksheets!!!) and some big-picture understanding. I wish they focused more on the understanding part and less on the details (personally I don't care what the difference is between clathrin and dynamin) but at least the lectures taught plenty of understanding, not only details. Dr. Lin is a nice guy, very funny sometimes, and good lecturer. TA's were not helpful and TA lectures were very confusing, but hopefully that was just this semester. Attendance is required Monday morning, which sucks, but other lectures can be skipped because they're recorded. The worksheets were also awful. But the textbook was good and I definitely learned A LOT. Definitely ask for points back after exams if you feel the grading wasn't fair, and definitely read the textbook, and definitely study the worksheets and weekly quizzes a lot before exams. Good luck!

Dr. Wu is an extremely nice professor, and she makes this very content-dense and challenging course significantly more manageable! She also truly wants all her students to succeed, offering a significant amount of extra credit points (up to 15+ pts possible!!! and this is WITHOUT including the exam wrapper!) I've overall had a pretty good experience in this class; There's no final (hooray), but it's important you do well on at least two midterms (1 is dropped and you have the chance to earn back points - up to 25% of what you lost - for Exam I), since exams make up ~60% of your grade. While the exams are open-note, they each cover A LOT of content, and much of it is application-based, as opposed to pure memorization, so you must have a firm understanding of the tested content to actually get a good grade. This class is definitely challenging and requires a significant amount of time dedicated to studying, but it's definitely manageable if you're up to the task! Kyle and Adena are both very helpful TAs. Kyle was very kind and great regarding answering homework/exam questions, also props to him for being an undergrad and just being an absolutely wonderful/informative TA! Adena was amazing with teaching the bioinformatics portion of BSCI410. I hadn't had prior R-language exposure, but Adena's R introduction lecture/office hours made coding significantly easier/more understandable even for someone without any previous coding experience! I personally found that attending lecture in person was not helpful; there's a lot of content, and Dr. Wu is a quick lecturer (definitely not her fault, given how much she covers)! However, lectures are all recorded, and you can attend via Zoom, so I'd attend asynchronously to answer clicker questions / listen to Dr. Wu in the background, and then watch the recording and take notes at my own pace to make sure I didn't miss anything important. This was definitely a time-consuming method, but it really helped me absorb the material a lot better, and the difference between my Exam I and Exam II/Exam III scores DEFINITELY showcased that (went from a D on Exam I without wrapper to an A- on Exam II). Overall, great class, but be aware that it does require a significant amount of focus to do well! If I had been taking a heavier course load this semester, I doubt I would have been able to dedicate as much time as I personally needed to achieve an A (which is why I'm giving a 4 instead of a 5).

This course was extremely challenging and negatively impacted my mental health. Despite attending GSS, completing practice exams, and consistently studying, I struggled to score above a 60 on the exams. The exams felt significantly more difficult than the practice material and required a level of speed and depth that was hard to manage. If possible, I strongly recommend taking a different professor for General Chemistry.

Maddie is probably one of the best TA's I will ever have in college. She was extremely helpful in the lab, whether that be helping you understand the procedure or calculations after the fact. She responds to emails wicked fast, and clarified any problems I had with post lab. Overall a really nice person and great TA.
In all honesty if you’re good with teaching it to yourself then she’s really not that bad, she’s very kind and her TA, Matt, is great. Aside from that she cannot teach at all.

There are no good professors for CHEM136 that I am aware of, so take this review with a grain of salt. Dr. White is clearly passionate about Chemistry and is knowledgeable on the subject. BUT... she is not an understanding professor and does not care about her students, making this class very unfair. I spend more time doing work for this class than CHEM135 (I ended CHEM135 with a 95% and CHEM136 with a 82%... make that make sense). The labs are extremely stressful because they don't make sense and the TA's have zero clue what's going on. Also, before each lab, you have to take a short "pre-lab quiz", for which they pull questions out of thin air and slap them onto a piece of paper (you'll be happy to get a 6 out of 10). Then comes the lab report. It's a living hell trying to figure out what the questions are asking, especially if you haven't taken AP Chem in high school. Each lab report takes me a minimum of 5 or 6 hours to complete (I once spent a good 8 hours on one and many tears were shed). Then comes the grades. The rubric for our lab reports is out of this world ridiculous. She takes off points if you don't draw the axis of your graphs with a ruler!!! And I got a 9 points off on a lab report which was 100% correct... all because I used 3 sig figs instead of 2 for my final answer calculations! And if this wasn't enough, you have a midterm and a final which are more of a guessing game than an actual test on knowledge (average lies around a 60%). Moving on... the only way you will manage to pass this class is if you go to her office hours and ask her as many questions about the lab as you can possible think of. I almost forgot to mention that because the grades are so bad in this class, she rounds the highest person up to an A+ and everyone else accordingly. Good luck and remember that C's get degrees :)

Dr. Hong isn't the worst professor, but if you have the choice to take someone more experienced, I would suggest doing so. With that being said, he is bearable. He is overall a fair professor despite going VERY fast during lectures. He also posts the homeworks and discussion worksheets, which you need to do for practice to pass his class. I would also suggest going to the GSS, those are very useful. With that being said, he does go FAST. He goes incredibly fast, and sometimes it is hard to keep up with him during lecture. I do find myself watching organic chemistry tutor at times due to his speed. However, he is always open to answering questions, especially during his lectures. Just make sure not to fall behind because he doesn't record lectures.

Genuinely one of the worst professors I’ve ever had. Sends emails out SUNDAY nights about what we need to do for lab the next week. I’d say reports are graded more strict than 132. There has been multiple occasions where I go in for office hours and the TAs will tell me my post labs are all correct but when I submit them I get a 10/20. Doesn’t seem like the TAs know how to do it either. I’ve also heard from multiple TAs that Dr koppel tells them to be as strict as possible with grading and give minimal points.

Yes Dr. Isaacs is a good person but his teaching abilities are okay, mediocre at best. Most of your learning will have to be from the textbook, which for me was very difficult. He barely does any practice questions in class just the one on his premade slides which I felt was never as hard as the questions on the exams. The best way to study imo is to read the whole textbook and pray for the best. The averages on exams were around 42-60%. I ended with a 60.67% which ended up being a B. Yes the curve is nice but try to avoid him if you can, unless you have many hours in your week to sit down and do every single textbook question. I honestly had a good shot at getting an A but the final exam was all MCQs (his first time doing that) and it was diabolical since no half credit. He thought that making his final all multiple choice would be easy for everyone but it was the opposite. Nothing could have prepared me for that exam, even the 50+ hours i spent in mckeldin. That being said, discussion section and review sessions with the TA Nick saved me so go to those. Only take Isaacs if you know you have time to read the textbook, otherwise save your time and pick someone else if doable.

Chem242 is, in my opinion, harder that Chem241, but not too too much worse. *Definitely* go to office hours though (with the nicest + most helpful TA you can find, not necessarily your TA). Some of those post-lab questions can kick your butt without help. My TA was lowkey incompetent (it seemed like he never read our lab manual, and he thought pH paper worked on dry powder) (it doesn’t) but it was fine anyways. I only met the actual professor one time because I went to his office hours but he was really nice. However, since you don’t have a choice in your prof or your TA, this review is mostly just to inform you that if you survived Orgo 1 lab, you should be fairly ok, and to say one more time GO TO TA OFFICE HOURS!!

Her class felt unorganized compared to my previous chemistry courses. This had some positives and negatives that I listed below. Pros Moving homework deadlines and 1 exam date (b/c the majority of the class agreed with delaying it) Extra credit opportunities Lots of office hours Discussion worksheets and TAs were very helpful Discussions are optional, and you can attend any of them. Cons: HWs are long and require external materials to be watched (her asynchronous lectures and CANs). Questions may be dropped or added within 1 day of the deadline. Limited study resources in Elms Lots of typos on HW that may/may not be publicly addressed to the class. There are lots of people in the office hours. I think I've never spent so much time in office hours to get nearly nothing out of it. There are so many people in her office hours that people often wait outside her office. I also don't think I understood her explanations well.

Schech is fine. You don't really need to go to the lecture to understand. Exams are pretty easy, you just need to go back to the notes (she posts her panopto video lectures) and do the practice exam basically. The average on the exam is like 85-90%. The only issue is some of the TAs grading the lab reports are very nitpicky and take points off for basically nothing, but that's not Schech's fault. Also, you can miss up to 3 labs without providing a "university-approved excuse," just contact your TA and Dr. Schech.

She is a super nice person but not the best at lecturing or teaching the class. Her slides are really good and you can learn a lot from the slides. She shows the slides and does live coding demos in class. If you pay attention in class and have decent prior knowledge of the topics you will be ok. Honestly not the best prof but if you can learn on your own and read slides you will be definitely good for 131.

I took Elias for 131 and 132 and I will say that he is definitely the best introductory CS professor anyone could ask for. I was very scared coming into UMD because I had pretty much no true coding experience (I had not even taken AP CS principles) and I had heard from various planetterp reviews and forums that this course would be difficult if I did not already have at least some background in CS. However, Elias made both of these courses a great experience. He truly cares about his students and takes time to talk about topics such as mental health. He also has a system set up so that there are nearly constant office hours making it very easy to get help with projects or leading up to exams. His lectures were also very engaging. He explained concepts very well (especially for someone with no prior knowledge) and was always very receptive to questions (as I used to ask a lot especially in 132), making sure his answers contained as much depth as possible. In addition to being a great teacher and having a system that makes it easy to get help, he also records lectures, provides a plethora of practice material for midterms and the final, and overall is just a very approachable person. Would definitely recommend.

If you want an easy grade without really learning anything, take Nelson. He tries to be funny, but that's not what I came to school for. I wish I had taken 216 with somebody who actually cares more about teaching than just being popular. I got an A, but I don't really feel prepared for upper level courses that might depend on 216.

I do NOT recommend taking 250 with Teli. I got a decent grade, but I seriously don't know what I'm doing. I went to a couple of 250 lectures given another professor and it was so much better. The other class actually held my interest and now I understand what 250 is supposed to be like. Teli's version of 250 is more like a middle school class than a course at a university. I wish I had taken somebody else.

PROS: - Very funny and engaging professor, I was rarely bored during lecture and actually liked going. - Homework assignments make up a great portion of the grade, making it easier to pass even if you slip up on an exam. - HW assignments are very interesting despite being vague. He might ask something like "here's a dataset, write me a report about the data," and it's up to the student to decide what to do from there. A lot of extra credit is given for creativity, effort, and generally impressing the grader, which helps boost your grade at the end of the semester. - Exam questions could pop up in data science interviews. They also force you to be well-prepared and understand the content. - Homeworks can be decent projects to put on your resume - Max is a pretty reasonable professor and is willing to help out, as long as you talk to him well ahead of deadlines. - Sometimes cancels class spontaneously, but this could also be perceived as a con since the class might fall off schedule - He gives LOTS of extra credit opportunities. I would say to do all of them; you might end up needing it at the end of the semester. Lots of it doesn't even take that long, it just involves you submitting notes for a lecture or taking a photo of you studying for an exam with a friend. CONS: - While he can be really unserious, some people might not like that style, since it can lead to distraction or falling off schedule - Exams are pretty hard and can sometimes be very poorly worded. Class averages for the first two midterms were not great (Exam 1 was roughly 66%, Exam 2 was 70%) - He can be pretty disorganized. Either he forgets to cover something in class, or just doesn't cover it at all since he spent too much time in class going on random tangents. - He takes pretty long to respond to emails. - You will need to do a lot of self teaching. He covers a little bit of pandas, but aside from that, not much code is covered at all. I had to teach myself how to use more pandas functions, Scikit-learn, and other important frameworks necessary for class. Other notes/takeaways: - Watch the 3Blue1Brown playlist on neural networks when you get to that part of the class, those were really helpful in understanding the concepts. Those concepts are also testable. - Start homework early to avoid late submission or cheating. - Do all the extra credit opportunities, they really don't take that long to do and could really help you out. Overall, he's a decent professor and I enjoyed taking the class with him.

He's not that great of a lecturer, but he's my favorite professor. He's just the best, but not the best at teaching. He's funny too :). Class in general is easy, the projects take a little while, so I'd to starting at least 2 days before the due date. It's annoying to have a project due soon when the autograder does not work right and the readme has 500 typos. This isn't Prof. Mamat's fault, though, I'm pretty sure it's Cliff's fault. The TA's were actually good unlike CMSC351.

Nelson is knowledgeable and teaches the material decently but he is unprofessional. He often distracts from the material and embarrasses students, like calling out a student for her insulin pump beeping. He shouldn't have to make jokes at the expense of a student to engage his class because not every student is comfortable being put on blast in front of the whole class. This behavior discourages students from coming to class and creates an uncomfortable environment for those that he picks on and students that have to watch. He does grade fairly and records lectures which is nice. He seems to care about students a lot but continues to act rudely towards them.
If she is co-teaching with Justin again -- 5/5. Her exams are more fair, and she is a very nice person and a lenient grader. Just study off of Justin's notes and do well on the midterms
Breaks the mold for CS teachers. New CS teacher that I have no issues with and responds to every question on Piazza with a quick and easy to understand explanation. Highly recommend.

Flipped classroom model yada yada yada. Judge yourself whether you will actually succeed in that type of environment. Marsh as a professor is knowledgeable and tries to do everything he can for his students. His slides are utterly useless in terms of actually learning what to do, so you will have to do most of the learning on your own (which really doesn't help in the flipped classroom model) or figure it out somehow, which leads me to the the biggest problem with this class: the projects. They are incredibly difficult, no two ways about it. Somehow I managed to complete them but oh boy was it stressful. I also am not really interested in the class content, so that definitely didn't help. Also, one thing to note is that this class HEAVILY leans into computer security rather than network security. Do not think this class's content will give you enough information comparable to 417.

Easy tests and hard projects. I feel like most 400 classes don't let you get your hands dirty with the projects and hold your hand with many of the assignments. This class basically rips off that bandage and expects you to learn C/C++ and make you write all the code yourself. You get to write many practical and useful projects compared to the other 400 classes I've taken so far. Projects (a2 onward) are stressful, but I have only myself to blame as I would start 2-4 days before the due date. As long as you start early and am confident in your coding skills, you will most likely do fine in this class. I enjoyed the content and teachings of Roy albeit sometimes a little boring.

After reading all of these opinions on the 7 exam structure, I wanted to join and say I actually really enjoyed it. This was one of my favorite CS classes ever. Instead of cramming for large exams with a bunch of different concepts, I was able to focus on just two at a time and actually learn! The exams line up very well with the practice problems and are not very difficult. The number of exams and the fact that Justin drops some is also very forgiving if you have an off week. Overall, Justin is an amazing lecturer and the structure of this class was very fair in my opinion. I learned a lot.
Super disorganized and lectures don't go anywhere near the kind of depth you would expect from a 400 level class, it was a struggle to learn anything at all

I genuinely wanted to learn this material, but the way the course was run made that almost impossible. It’s hard to express how much I dislike this course. It’s structured very poorly: it’s extremely fast-paced with almost no room to actually retain the material. The assignments don’t reflect what you need to know to do well on the exams, and the textbooks are pretty unhelpful if you’re new to ML. I’m not even going to say much about the grading (yes, it’s very punitive, likely due mostly to the TAs) because others have already covered that. The instructor seems to assume that if one person gets an A on the midterm, then everyone should be able to get an A, which completely ignores the reality that students juggle many responsibilities. It’s not just “do research,” “teach,” eat, and sleep. Her teaching style ends up overwhelming students and reinforcing unnecessary competition, especially coming from someone who didn’t go through the same level of modern academic pressure, unstable economy, or constant distractions. Overall, the class was mentally draining because of the uncertainty around how to actually learn and retain the material, what to expect on exams, and how to find reliable resources for long-term understanding. By the second midterm, the stress had taken a significant toll on, I’m sure, the majority of the class. Amazing and thank you!

this class was absolutely atrocious. the participation quizzes were not in fact graded on participation/completion, but rather on accuracy. the weekly readings are tedious and dense, and the reading quizzes themselves are a monstrosity. all of the projects are taken from another university, so the codebase is super deep and complex. there is very little guidance on implementing the required methods, and the difficulty of the projects do not match the information learned from the reading quizzes. onto the next: exams. the most vile questions are cooked up to test every single edge case of our knowledge. algorithms are confusingly modified to test if we have a master's level of understanding of databases, and the questions are specifically tailored to trip us up. the other reviews below can confirm this, abadi seems to find great joy in this. cool class and important concepts, but i did not anticipate this class to be the hardest class i have ever taken at my university. truly tragic when trying to load balance your schedule and this abomination of a class appears out of nowhere.

I usually believe that when people review teachers, they're a bit too pessimistic when they give so many professors a 1 star. I've had fabled terrifying professors such as Yoon for 216, and while I wouldn't say such experiences were pleasant, I usually find stuff of value that the class and teacher bring to the table. Before I had Professor Aloimonos, I doubted I would ever skip a class, because even though it's tempting, there's still stuff of value to it. So with the preamble out of the way, time to rant about this class. There has never been a more disorganized class in my life. Frankly, it's a stretch to even call this class a "class", because Alomoinos is so out of the loop for everything, and the class is basically just run by TAs. Slides are quite terrible and poorly written and organized, and project directives are EXTREMELY vague and you won't know what you're doing most of the time. Piazza is fairly unresponsive and solely answered by TAs. All projects are group but insanely long and will definitely take 10+ hours even if you're a strong programmer. Each lab comes with a report you have to write about what you did. The lectures provided by Aloimonos are nigh uninterpretable, as his accent and monologues go far off any actual content that's useful to the labs you'll eventually have to do. There was one midterm for the class, and since so few people went to class at this point/people didn't understand what was going on, an MC test where you didn't even have to answer every question, had a terrible average. Even worse, some questions had incorrect answers in the answer key, and students had to argue to deal with how inaccurate/vaguely worded the questions were. Most people will probably look at this class and think to themself, "But, anon, the average is so high. Why wouldn't I take this class?" And, sure, labs are mostly graded as 100s and despite the midterm, extra credit + no final + 10% piazza participation leads to a high average. But why would you want to subject yourself to so much stress, and so much effort, for a class you'll struggle to learn in? Also a side note: although a lot of the TAs aren't that responsive, the head TA, Naitri, is definitely the highlight of this class as she genuinely posts guides to the labs, has useful office hours, and actually runs this class fairly well. However, this does not excuse how poorly managed the class is as a whole, as well as how much Professor Alomoinos's non-teaching makes this class difficult. Anyways, in short, please do not take this class.

This course is literally the continuation to CMSC330 but more. Uses functional language (but in Racket not Ocaml) to develop compiler and interpreter. Professor is a very smart, enthusiastic, and kind professor. Notes are posted online and the lectures are recorded, which is very helpful for review. Projects can be tedious but are manageable if you dont procrastinate. Exams are TAKE HOME and 24-hour! This is very different but I liked it tbh. Note: the 1st exam is easy but the 2nd is much more difficult. I spent like a straight 12 hours working on it to pass all cases. They say that you should be able to finish in a normal class period but that's not even remotely true if you want a good grade lol.

Have you ever wanted to waste a semester learning nothing, but still be so stressed about a class you nearly get an ulcer? Do you want a teacher who will be rude and condescending to you and ignore all your concerns? Is your life missing a teacher who is utterly incapable of explaining the material and steadfastly refuses to answer your questions in any comprehensible way? Dr. Li demonstrated every single day in class that he did not understand the material any better than the students did, or that if he did, he was so utterly incapable of communicating the material that we just assumed that lecture was the first time he was seeing it. Asking him questions didn't help as, assuming he didn't just ignore your question, he regularly failed to answer it in any meaningful way or even rephrase the confusing material in a way that could be better understood. Lecture slides are utterly useless for learning due to being incomprehensible. Going to TAs to learn the material doesn't help either as they don't understand it either - though that's not their fault; he so completely fails to impart even the smallest nugget of information on whoever he is talking to that even they don't understand what was going on in the class Often the TAs were forced to just give out the answers left and right to students or almost the entire class would fail. We regularly had 3-4 projects assigned to us at a time on top of regular homeworks. Who cares? Not Dr. Li. You doing poorly on an exam is just another example that proves his belief that students at UMD are idiots (literally something he has said to his TAs). If I could give this man fewer than 1/5 stars I would - he's one of the few professors on PlanetTerp with 1-star reviews across the board. Do yourself a favor and avoid him at all costs.

I dont know why people give him terrible reviews. For 434, he was pretty good. I barely attended his lectures, but this class seemed quite interesting. Has a pretty cool psychological aspect and relates to the real world in a way we don't usually realize. The class is structured about 40% exams, 40% semester long group project, and 10% attendance. Roughly. The exams are all very very easy. I studied the day before only by just going through his practice questions he posted and I got A's on all of them. The semester long project is not that bad if you have a good group. I luckily had a group that knew what they were doing and could code in kotlin so they carried me. The reason I got a C is because I didn't do much on the project so when your groupmates decide after each project phase how much each person did, I got a bad review. Golub is a pretty chill professor.

If you are a procrastinator, AVOID AVOID AVOID. This last month has been so ridiculously stressful. I really really really regret taking this course. If you're not a procrastinator, then it's an Easy A.

Homeworks are hard and can take quite some time to figure out a solution, but you have 2-3 weeks to do them. Exams were difficult as well, but it seems like there is a generous curve at the end of the course (75% got me a B). Regarding the lectures, they feel very useful as Childs will go through the material thoroughly and is good at checking for questions and answering them.

Great class. Teaching material was pretty good, detailed slides using wolfram. Todd worked at wolfram for 15 years, he was able to use it for lectures. Exams were fair, homework grading was easy and fast. Really goes to show that the math department actually cares about students. Thankfully this semester 456 was under control by the math department. If it was taught by CS it would have terrible teaching, terrible TAs, and terrible grades.

Hajiaghyi has been a nightmare as a professor. When exams don't match class material and your grades are determined by how well you do against others, it feels a little bit contradictory to his constant talk about wanting everybody to succeed as that is literally impossible when a third of the class is guaranteed to get a 50% on two of the three total projects. Super easy and straightforward class, very similar to MATH206 where the class is largely self taught but is simple

I feel like he relies way too much on his TA's for the class and doesn't really care for the class at all. You pretty much have to self-learn everything which is pretty hard if you don't have much experience with coding.

Horrendous teacher, don't get how she is 4.3 stars. I took her because I got a recommendation from a friend, as well as the good PlanetTerp reviews. She creates a GroupMe for the class, then accuses half the class for cheating because we asked questions in it? She makes the subject matter really straight forward. Lectures are very clear, and she always posts class notes. Her exams are also fairly easy. The only issue I ever had with her was that it took her a VERY long time to grade exams.

Dr Fernandes was a good teacher overall. His biggest flaw was that he relied heavily on the TAs to teach methods discussed in class. The final is daunting, but definitely possible to get an A on if you go over enough past finals and understand the processes behind the questions given. Super nice, easy professors. Exams were always very fair and didn't require alot of computation. Pretty straightforward. Exam weighting is also great, he drops 2 lowest quizzes and makes your lowest midterm weigh half the others. Best prof to take calc 3 w imo. My test averages were like 97s.

Junyan is funny as shit and dresses like an anime mc. He teaches well in general, but also goes really fast which makes it hard to keep up, and has pretty questionable handwriting. That being said, his exams are pretty reasonable (difficulty-wise), and are very similar to assigned textbook problems. Most of my learning was outside of class by watching Justin Olav Wyss-Gallifent on youtube. Overall nice guy and would generally recommend.

HE IS NOT A GOOD PROFESSOR! His mumbles during his lectures, makes many mistakes, and goes way too fast. The first midterm was unnecessarily difficult (class avg of 52%) and only 2 problems (each with part a and b). it's kind of crazy because each midterm is 200 points (20% of the entire grade) He does give a retake opportunity for each midterm, but they aren't much easier. The second midterm was much better (class avg 76). The class is curved such that an 85% is an A (A- if right on the border), 75% is a B and so on. There are 4 MATLAB projects which are very easy and in class quizzes that are directly from the suggested problems almost every week usually 10pts each (Midterms are 200, Final is 400). Otherwise, there isn't any homework. The textbook that he uses is mid, Paul's Online Math Notes was a much more useful resource. Attendance isn't mandatory but you risk missing an in-class quiz as he usually doesn't announce them.

The workload was extremely manageable and the resources available were super helpful. It is obvious that Dr. Gruber cares a lot about his students and provides his students with everything they need to succeed. This class was taught wonderfully.

Pros: Pretty nice person Class is not hard at all for a math400 Pretty receptive to feedback IMO, this is her first time teaching at UMD Cons: Lectures are kind of all over the place, it's hard to learn/glean anything from them She also just reads off Justin's notes, once I realized this I never showed up for lectures Groupworks SUCK, they are done in groups of three but what always happens is one person does matlab one person writes and if you are not one of those you are kind of just sitting there. easy points but sometimes the most boring hr of my life Some of the homeworks are SO LONG Overall shes not the best, but if you have her you will be fine. She also improved over the semester and I can see her being a lot better in the future

Hands down on of my all time favorite professors. Great lecturer, makes the content easy to understand, very responsive to email, and genuinely cares about his students doing well. You can expect a weekly homework that takes about an hour max, 3 midterms, and a final. The exams tend to be tough, but he curves generously at the end of the semester.

This was my favorite class this semester. I really liked lectures, he was very approachable in office hours, homeworks were sufficiently challenging without feeling overboard most of the time, the content was interesting to me. I don't know, this class just did it for me. I talked to some people about taking this class and not having taken MATH403 yet, and a few have questioned me for doing so. While basic content from that class may be helpful for this class, MATH403 is in no way an implicit prerequisite for this professor's MATH405 (it may be for some sections, though I don't know personally). Positivity is hard to write about, so I'll put a few things I didn't quite like about this class here. For one, homeworks are physically handed in during class. I do all my work digitally, and printers are my worst nightmare, so this bugged me quite a bit, even though I attended every class anyways. Exams are heavily weighted, as each midterm is 25%, and the final is 40%, with the remaining 10% being homeworks. This isn't quite as bad as it could be, as the exams were rather easy all things considered, and each of them come with a bit of extra credit, but it's something to keep in mind if exams aren't your strongsuit. The textbook we used, Linear Algebra Second Edition by Hoffman and Kunze, isn't bad by any means, but I didn't like some aspects of it. There are some problems in the book which aren't the most clear due to having wonky English, using terminology which hasn't been fully established (independent set comes to mind, where the book means linearly independent set without first establishing that fact, where independent set is a term from graph theory), or having odd symbol usage (using \to instead of \mapsto for mappings, for example). In general, I generally prefer how Linear Algebra Done Right by Sheldon Axler presents information, and used it as a second reference on a few occasions throughout the course. Finally, one particular lecture after exam 2 felt very rushed, which was rather annoying given that a homework on the topic was assigned that day and due the next class (usually, a full week is given to do ahttps://youtu.be/XjZHAa4hR68 homework). For me, my gripes are minor in the grand scheme of things. I highly recommend this professor for MATH405.

As other reviews have mentioned, Dong Quan is a great teacher when it comes to explaining and developing concepts. He is always willing to go out of his way to recap unfamiliar or forgotten material, and will answer any question asked in detail. Furthermore, he is very nice and wants everybody to succeed doing everything in his power to help every student get good grades. The problem with this, though, is that there is a notable difference between students learning material and getting good grades. Graded exercises are made trivial after discussed in class (often before their due date, and in detail) and due to a generous grading structure, nobody in the class had to take the final since a take-home midterm was half our grade. The grading structure was the top two categories out of homework, midterm, and final, each of the two weighted to be 50% of our final grade. I don't think anybody ended the course without an A+, though, and certainly not without an A because so many assignments became copy-and-paste from his notes in class. This resulted in students receiving good grades without the need for them to learn or understand material. Looking at some exams in the testbank, for example, I'm lost on many of the questions, with question formats we've never seen. I'd attribute this to a mix of a focus on theory from Dong Quan and a lack of rigor to the course. While Dong Quan is great at teaching, one of the fundamentals of learning is practice, and without any graded assignments that actually required students to do anything other than copy and paste notes, it's hard to say that anybody came out of the class knowing a ton more than when they entered. On a separate note, I want to verify his habit to extend due dates and his somewhat frequent online lectures. There's nothing necessarily bad about either of these, but both are something to be aware of. In conclusion, take the class if all you care about is your final grade. In this case, you will get the grade you want with minimal effort. Otherwise, opt for another more rigorous teacher.

The BEST math professor I've encountered. Panos is extremely knowledgable and interacts with everyone so well each lecture. I love how he never reads straight from the textbook, but instead tries to derive every proof himself, which really helped me understand how to problem solve and think about things. He also made each exam take-home including the final, making this class not very stressful unlike other professors. Highly recommend.

Solid professor, he's definitely not the professor described in the MATH410 review from a few years ago. He engages with the class frequently and likes it when people are on time to class. His exams are also very fair (he sends out practice problems and sometimes has review sessions for them), and he even added an optional third midterm in case you wanted to improve your grade. He did make the final worth 45% of the overall grade, but if the difficulty is similar to the midterms, I think it will be fine. If you are the type of person that goes to class, I would recommend Professor Berhanu for analysis courses.

Levermore is cool - as long as you can endure his snarky attitude. His lecture is fine, but I find the pace a bit slow. That said, this man should be banned from teaching new courses. He couldn't finish writing the homework on time for most of the time of the semester, so we had 5 psets for spring break and 4 psets for final's week. That was just not very reasonable. The exams were take-homes because of the pandemic. While the first exam was long and easy (the format was similar to the hw with the workload doubled), the second one was really tedious (he picked the hardest + longest problem from each hw and compiled them together). That was one of the instances when I look at my solution and wonder how on earth would the instructor have the mental power to read through my solution. He graded things very leniently at the end, I'm not sure if it was because he felt sorry for the way he bombarded us with giant hw packages or he's just lenient. Anyway.. the material is very interesting, I recommend learning some harmonic analysis on your own if you get a chance. The text used was Wickerhauser - alright but not the best for self-study (<- so you can't learn everything by reading the book and not attending lectures).

The sweetest guy. He is so excited about this class, and does his best to make it interesting. He is also very accommodating, as other reviews have mentioned. I joined the class a week late, and he gave me more than enough time to catch up, all you have to do is be transparent and ask for help. I have never taken physics once in my life before this, so it was certainly a struggle. You need to put in plenty of time. He does NOT use a textbook which is frustrating, so buy the suggested book (it is NOT a waste of money). He goes super quick in his lectures, so you definitely need to review by yourself. Also, he provides the formula sheets, you do NOT get to make your own. So make sure you understand the formulas because the formula sheets give very little. You also have to infer on a lot of things, but if you get the hang of the problems you'll see, you'll do fine. DO THE HOMEWORK, there will be some crazy questions from there that will be on the exam. Overall, I would recommend him for someone who just needs PHYS121 for their major.
Lectures can be really dry but she's super nice and accommodating. Gives 20+ points worth of extra credit questions for each exam.

I know a lot of people have said this is a chill class and most people can easily get an A, but if you hate physics like me, don't relax and take this class too lightly. Even though exam averages were pretty high (70-75), I felt this class was the bane of my academic career simply because I felt like the practice problems weren't enough to grasp the boring material. I couldn't ever appreciate what I was learning, but nobody cares about that anyway. You could tell Severson couldn't care less if you even understood what he was rambling about. Labs and hw were outright pointless with some problems even dating back to 2002, believe it or not. And even though exams were much, much better than they were in 131, I had to really study and lock in to get close to the average and then do well on the final. I honestly learned more from Khan Academy than anything in this class, so if you want digestible problems and actually understand the material, this would be my most significant study help. Overall, if your mind manages to fathom physics, you'll be fine. But if it's more like a chore, as it was for me, just take a breath, pick up your credits, and move on.

Losert is a good professor. I just hate the life science physics classes. Losert is passionate about physics and he can be funny at times as well. However, the head TA taught 1/3 of the lectures because Losert was at a conference like every other week. He does TopHat questions just like 131, and some of them are graded for accuracy, but he'll literally tell you the answers in class so as long as you're there, you will get it right. ExpertTA homework was time consuming and annoying. It's literally impossible to fail this class. You don't need to know anything about the content going into the exams because you get a double-sided formula sheet and the curve is insane, and you can bs enough to get a solid grade. Also, the exams have retakes, where your new grade is the average of the original and the retake (although I've heard the retakes are much harder). Exam 2 was nothing like the practice. Labs are easier than 131 - once you get through the couple of harder lab reports at the beginning, the rest are easy and don't require a whole lab report - just answering questions. It's also highly dependent on if your group members actually do the work. Overall, I've learned nothing in this class. 131 and 132 are a joke. I would've been better off taking the non-life science physics courses.

Absolute trash. Take heidarian. Tests are a little hard but not insane. Except for the final, the average was a 58. Grading is very harsh. Lectures are so boring you might fall asleep. If you fall asleep worry not, as the lectures are so useless for learning the content and how to actually solve problems that you will have missed nothing.

This lab is strange because it seems like it should be a corequisite for physics 1, not physics 2. Since almost everything was review, it was very easy, and it was possible to finish each lab at least an hour ahead of time. (Note that Severson was never there in-person, only the TAs.)

Pretty easy professor and class I just didn't really study. My final grade was an 81% and ended with a C+ because of the weird grading that he does which was annoying. But the tests were multiple choice and you get a cheat sheet - 5 for the final which was insane. Lecture kind of sucked I only stuck it out the first half of the semester, but the online textbook helped a lot to understand the harder concepts but really all you need is to understand the homeworks. The first test was very easy - 85% average. The second test was insane around 50% average you need to actually understand everything fully. The third test was fine with around a 75% average, the final was also easy pulling directly from the midtems almost completely with another high % average. Recommend him over Skuja for sure there are no quizzes with Baden unlike Skuja and the tests are much easier.

Dr. Turpen is simply an amazing professor. She really cared about us learning the physics while not making the class too difficult. Lectures were easy to follow and we had in-class participation quizzes that really helped to reinforce what we were learning. The homeworks were never too difficult or long, and exams were fair. If Dr. Turpen is teaching 371 for your semester, you'll be in for a treat.

So I had a lot of problems with Gates' teaching style. First is that, being a theoretical physicist whose career is based on quantum mechanics, he is a bit too good at the concepts in this class. So he would often go over material too quickly for everyone to understand it. Also, he was frequently out of town so we would often have a substitute which was not a horrible thing but I kind of like consistency. However, my biggest problem was his grading. He gave several quizzes throughout the semester and one of those was the day before Thanksgiving. How many people go to class that day? He also refused to let people make the quiz up. On both of the midterms, the front page said you have 2 hours to complete the test. We had 1 hour classes. So pretty much no one finished the tests and the grades reflected that. Even if we had had enough time the tests were incredibly difficult and the grades still would have been awful (virtually all the questions were incredibly difficult unless you knew some obscure math trick). These poor grades are reflected by the grade distribution. I think that over 60% of the class got a C or below, including about 1/4 of the class getting D's or F's. In my opinion, that is an absurd distribution that reflects an awful grade policy. That said, he was good about answering questions so if you knew what you didn't understand you could ask for help easily enough. But I really didn't know what I didn't know until after the tests.

Yakovenko is one of the better professors in the physics department, probably the second best physics prof. I have had after Hall. He lectures directly from the book, but I think his lectures are informative and helpful even though many people decided to skip them. His grading scheme is also very unique: 50% homework and 50% tests, and there are two tests, each counting 25%. He does assign a lot of homework though, and it is difficult, although the problems are not his own but are from the book. He sometimes makes up additional parts to questions which are pretty straightforward. Tests were impossible, however. I think the averages were below 50%. The curve at the end of the semester was something like above 70% weighted homework and tests was an A. I would recommend taking a class with Yakovenko, because he is one of the better lecturers in the department and the grading scheme really rewards those who work hard on their homework. You end up learning a lot in the class.

In the interest of full disclosure I am now working for Professor Anlage. That said I took his class before I started working for him and I really liked the class, which is odd for a 400 level physics class. Unlike many (or most) physics teachers, Professor Anlage actually gave a reasonable amount of work. I was pretty much always able to finish the entire homework assignments within a few hours of when I started. Also, he gave one extra credit problem per homework and they were often not difficult. In addition, all of his tests seemed to have a reasonable degree of difficulty. I think all the test problems were fairly interesting and not overly difficult. I think the averages were like 80, 72, and 70 for the 2 midterms and final respectively (my previous physics class had been with Professor Gates and the first test had the cutoff for a B as a 30%). I don't know how much he ended up curving the class but upon checking the grade distribution, I saw that only 2 people in the class got below a C and about 2/3 of the class got A's and B's which seems like a good distribution. That said I didn't think the lectures were overly interesting. One thing I have noticed is that as you get further along in Physics, the Physics becomes more and more abstract. So you really didn't come out of lectures feeling as though you learned anything real. I generally felt that I could solve a problem easily enough, but that problem would probably not have a strong basis in reality. However, one of the best things about Professor Anlage is that he always stayed after class for however long people were there to ask questions. There were several times where I stayed to ask something for over half an hour and he never seemed like he was rushed (unless another class started entering). Tl; dr: Take 410 with him because you will almost definitely pass and you will have a thorough understanding of the material although you may feel as though the material is irrelevant.

Very nice and sweet. She really wants her students to scared, and was always willing to go over concepts that people did not understand. Class consists of two exams, a final, r coding assignments, and homework assignments. The thing about this class, it is not difficult at all, and Khurana does a good job at teaching it. Just make sure to stay on top of the r assignments as those are not talked about in lecture but rather discussion. Overall very easy class and Khurana is very nice. If she is available for the class, don’t think twice. Exams are also very easy.

I watched my degree evaporate before my eyes on the final. Please don't take this man if your life depends on it. His exams were nothing like the HW, quizzes, or practice exams he gave us. He told us point estimators were not going to be a major topic of the final since we only learned it for a week, but then proceeded to make it 25% of the final exam, which is worth 40% of your grade. Pincus is a nice dude though and will answer all your questions. He also only reads off the slides and his lectures aren't more helpful than looking through a textbook
Easiest A of my life, but also the most frustratingly pointless class I have ever taken. Do not take Anurag Dey, especially for a course you want to use as a prerequisite for future courses.
Great TA. Very lenient. Very through in grading. Talked to him once, very humorous guy.

Took STAT420 and MATH410 at the same time, Fernandes is honestly the GOAT for any STAT class. His exams are mirror copies of the homework, and will NEVER give you anything on the exam that you haven't seen before. He spends a lot of time helping you look at the "bigger picture", and helps you solidify your understanding of the statistical process. He's great. Class is trivial.

STAT430 is really a light class content wise. Its just a review of STAT401 + learning to do automate statistical tests using SAS. However, she makes it way harder than it needs to be. She is incredibly disorganized and sometimes doesnt release the weekly homeworks until late in the week. The first exam is incredibly simple (just basic SAS procedures), but the 2nd exam is incredibly disorganized and is way too long to cover in a 50 minute class. She also gives no partial credit for the SAS portion. She is not communicative at all and her lectures are particularly useless. She's not a bad person, but she isn't particularly understanding at all and can come across as very condescending when asking questions. Overall, this class is very doable. But she makes it way more painful than necessary. I'd say to avoid her if you can, but you'll live as long as you're prepared for the disorganization and will especially be fine if you have programming experience.

DO NOT TAKE RANKIN. please. you have been warned. i will try to sum everything up in bullet points. in terms of the exams: - exams are online on a lockdown browser - her exam style is that of upper level bio courses. - the format of questions is extremely confusing and often has many answer choices (two of the above, three of the above, all of the above, none of the above) for EVERY question. not one question is straight forward. It’s almost like she designs them for failure. - we did so bad on the first exam she had to give us a retake. - you have 45 minutes for about 40 questions. - the questions are extremely long. im talking a paragraph PER question. - almost all questions are conceptual applications and do not directly apply to what we learned in class AT ALL. - lots of math questions with no calculator! - zero practice problems to prepare for the exam. like none. - she makes these huge study guides that do not contain any helpful content actually found on the exam - lots of material on the exam involved slides or IMAGES on slides that were completely skipped during lecture. - she will literally write the scientific name of a creature instead of the common name so you dont know what she’s talking about. brother i dont know the latin name for an earthworm STOP IT! - the averages are failing - no curves! she does award maybe 10 or so points of partial credit back though. - she does not accept criticism about the exam and will tell that to you to your face <3 in terms of the class itself: - every lecture is just her reading off dense slides - many times, slides were not posted before lecture - the simbio tutorials are the “homework” and are extremely long. they take HOURS each, and multiple were due in one day. not to mention they did not help prepare us for the exam at all. she actually said verbatim that some of the simbio textbook was inaccurate. - the grade distribution on canvas was wrong the whole semester. we were unable to know our grades in the class for the whole semester. - we each paid about forty dollars for point solutions polling software. its like kahoot but graded and she never gives you the access code. many of us got zeroes in our grade book despite participating in all polls. when we asked her about it she said to “contact the point solutions company” because she didnt know what was wrong. - she provided no avenue to help us improve our grades despite very low exam averages. in short, she wants you to fail. i dont think she’s evil, i just think she doesn’t know how to teach an intro level class. the TAs were extremely unhelpful as well. if you end up like me and dont catch on until its too late to drop, here’s my personal advice - dont just copy whats on the slides during class, unless that’s truly how you learn best. either sit and pay attention to what she’s saying or annotate the slides as she is talking. - do not spent too much time on the simbio assignments. they are essentially useless. i think only 2 questions of all 3 exams was based on the simbio. - use the optional Hillis et. al textbook that she mentions in the syllabus. it is more helpful than the simbio at actually explaining concepts - use flashcards to memorize definitions. there’s a lot of them. - ask ai to make conceptual practice problems and type k questions for the unit you are learning. - do not cram the night before! please. - dont beat yourself up about your grades. its truly not your fault. good luck and god speed. you should start praying from now.

She's not that bad. She's pretty fair and if you study a certain way you'll be fine. She's an icon/girl boss so theres bonus points and i can tell shes overqualified. so everything about her not being so good is true. it’s not necessarily about the way she teaches, but it’s about the lack of content given to us to prepare for exams. this class is very textbook heavy, which is a shame because the content is actually interesting. being asked to read 30 to 40 pages of a book every week only to maybe get asked about it once on the exam isn’t worth it. but no matter how good you know the information she’s not good at writing test questions that are coherent and clear. If there is any single review you listen to, let it be this one. If there is ANY other way to take this class, and I mean any other way, I urge you to take the other option. Dr. Friedman is a rude and impatient man. He teaches you concepts as if you should already know them, and going to his office hours doesn't help, as it seems as though he doesn't want to help you.
