The main issue I have with this class is the RIDICULOUS amount of knowledge you need to know for each of the lab practicals. In the span of about two weeks, it is expected of you to learn intricate details, most of which you don't even get tested on. At the same time, the allotted 2 hours and 50 minutes is way too long for the "lab," where its just the TA reading off the slides and dumping too much information all at once. This class requires way more memorization than what's actually tested. For example, she expects you to learn over 100 bone markings and over 60 muscles (which you also have to memorize the origin, insertion, and the action for) to answer a total of 25 questions. I also didn't like how the exams were structured, where there were stations with a piece of paper to answer for the most part. Throughout that test, I kept thinking how I could have easily utilized the time better by reviewing other questions and/or moving ahead to the more difficult questions. This "lab" felt more like a glorified lecture with another set of exams rather than applying concepts learned in class to a real-life model. I like BSCI 201 overall, but this "lab" kills the fun of this class.

I absolutely love this class and Dr. O'Brien does an amazing job at explaining the hard concepts. While there is a lot of information to memorize, it is Anatomy 2 so what else can you expect? I'm not sure why a lot of the reviews say she is rude, if you go to her office hours she is extremely helpful and easy to talk to. She gives many opportunities for extra credit and you can get one every class just by answering questions which she asks a lot of (you do not have to answer correctly). She drops some of the assignments at the end of the semester which raises your grade. The only thing is this class is at 8 am, so be sure to be prepared for that.

Dr. Karen was nice and helpful, but I'm not gonna lie this was one of my least favorite classes (and I usually love biology). The lectures were long (usually 60 slides) and the things on the slide were different from what she was saying (so you have to pay attention to both). Halfway through the semester, I stopped attending because she records the lectures and I just started watching those. DO NOT take notes from scratch, it is wayy too much work. Highly recommend using an ipad and importing the slides into a notetaking app like goodnotes for annotations. She doesn't give any practice tests or extra material for the test, but she does allow a cheat sheet. It is a good way to study because you can condense and organize all the material. If you write small and highlight, you can get a lot out of the cheat sheet. The tests were a lot easier than I thought as long as you spend the time studying before. The material tho was very much memorization based and all the units felt very disconnected, which made it harder to study for the final. Overall, a very heavy class but you should be able to manage if you are willing to put a lot of work in.

Honestly, it's not going to be like any bio you have ever taken. 7 questions, all free response, worth 200 points. No MC, nothing. He's a little less bad than our other option, but I genuinely would avoid him. It is by the grace of God I am going to pass this class, it is worth finding Jesus because this class will give you no hope!!!! God is truly the only hope carrying me through this class.

This class was more challenging than I anticipated, no doubt about it. Still, I think a lot of the super low reviews are from people who didn't put in the necessary time for this class or people who don't know how to adapt to a different classroom style and got a nasty awakening. Yes the flipped classroom model sucks, lectures always felt disorganized because it was literally just clicker questions, but that just means this class is more of a self-study type which isn't SO unusual in college. I wouldn't say the exams were necessarily brutal, yes, they were riddled with small typos/mistakes, but a lot of it boiled down to whether or not you could apply the knowledge learned from lab and lecture. The lab aspect of this class really helps to buffer your grade, while there's a lot of busy work, the small 10, 15, 20 point assignments add up and help you out in the end. I didn't do great on the first exam (low C), did slightly above average on the second exam (high B) and final (low B), but was still able to end up with an A- due to lab assignments. It's really important to have at least a basic understanding of lab tests and experiments, since they make up at least 20-30% of exams, but my TA always provided lab slides, and the protocols are all posted on ELMS. It also helps if your lab group is competent. I got lucky and we were able to divide work evenly, so no one ended up completing the entirety of an assignment on their own...but I heard some horror stories from friends in other sections. My TA was a godsend, and Dr. Buchner's TAs are half the reason why I decided to give him three stars. Along with checking in with groups during labs, she was always willing to stay after lab if we ended early to answer questions, was a quick grader, and responded quickly to emails. This may be more of a Dr. Buchner thing, since he was also understanding with extensions, but my TA was super lenient on late submissions, even for major assignments, and would help walk me through the rubric if me or my group mates were confused. The one thing that was kind of frustrating was that none of the TAs had a good understanding of what exams were going to be like, since this was Dr. Buchner's first semester lecturing since exams were switched back to paper. I think future semesters will be better since the TAs will have more exposure to the in-person exams, but the exam blindness, especially going into Exam I, was extremely stressful. I think it's insanely unfair for people to make comments on Dr. Buchner's mental state. While this class was disorganized at times, like him forgetting to print at least 30 final exams, he is understanding if he sees that you're making an effort in the class. Not my favorite professor of all time, but he's not a demonic, hellish tyrant. If you put in the effort and have a good TA and lab group, you'll do fine.

This class was very interesting. Prof. F does a really good job lecturing and keeping everything clean and captivating. He will explicitly tell you what will and will not be on the exams, and the general format of the class was very well put together. highly recommend.

• content is kinda difficult, especially if you're taking it before mamphys and never properly understood neuro stuff • don't slack off bc it's not an easy class to finesse • he's sweet tho (and fair-ish)

Dr. Wu is one of the most supportive and genuinely caring professors I’ve had at UMD. From the start of BSCI410, she has been approachable, responsive via email, and always available on Piazza to discuss questions or concerns. Her lectures are well-structured with clear diagrams and speaker notes, and the availability of recorded lectures with subtitles made reviewing material much easier. She also is just a cool person to talk to and get to know more about. By no means was this course easy, but putting in the time definitely pays off. She's definitely considerate when it comes to exams and grades - she gave lots of projects to bring up grades and extra credit opportunities. If you want to learn more about molecular genetics, I would recommend taking this class. Exams are open note but don't help that much so its much better just to learn from the Ta's and understand it yourself.

If there is any review you listen to, let it be this one. If there is ANY possible other professor you can take, I URGE you, BEG you to take any other option. Dr. Friedman is rude and runs through topics as if you have already learned them in depth. Yes, you should be expected to have a simple understanding of chemistry and remember things from high school, but the amount that I had to learn on my own was honestly diabolical. I spent probably over 10 hours a week on CHEM 131 (not including lab), simply by attending lectures, going to GSS twice a week, and going to office hours and discussions, doing the homework, and teaching myself. I am generally a straight-A student, and got an A+ in my chemistry class in high school. In this class, I worked my actual ass off for weeks, and didn't see the results I wanted since he would test us on the rare niche exceptions. I learned new things just by looking at his old exams. Be prepared to memorize the most unnecessary stuff and spend hours on the homework, while totally ruining your self-esteem. He is insulting and rude, going to his office hours did not help, instead it made me feel small and stupid. The ONLY pro is that his curve is very generous. I genuinely learned everything from Amy, the GSS leader, and Chad's prep on YouTube. I did not miss a single lecture, and it did not help. He is rude and cannot teach, though he clearly really does know what he's talking about. He blames his low averages on his students not trying, though that is not the case. My main complaint with this course and lab coordinator is that the rubrics for post-lab assignments are incredibly nit-picky and points are taken off for errors that are impossible to anticipate. There is almost no specific directions in this entire course, and I do not blame the TAs. The lab coordinator is mostly to blame.

I HIGHLY recommend taking this class if you're interesting in learning about data science and being prepared for data science interviews. His exams are very much pulled from what those interviews could be. I studied by taking notes on things that didn't make sense the first time I learned them, until they made sense, over and over and it has worked. I feel like a lot of people tried to study using practice exams, but that's not super helpful since his exams are different from one another. Practice exams in this course should be more like a last checkpoint / once over before the exam, not a sole study tool. These were probably the most entertaining lectures I've ever been to. Max is also a super nice, thoughtful, and funny person who is clearly trying very hard to help us. He takes time to explain why he's structuring the course in the way that he does during class. He even added an assignment at the end structured for us to be able to put it as an impressive project on our resume.
